Save to update Unity

pages.text:
Chickxel is a pixel art editor for games (especially Unity 2D). Frames, layers and tags (animations) are stored in a .chickxel project, and saving also produces a PNG sprite sheet and a Unity .meta. You don't need to install .NET or anything else.
OS Download (latest version) Run
Windows 10/11 Chickxel-windows-x64.zip Unzip and double-click Chickxel.exe
macOS 12 or later, Apple Silicon (M1 and later) Chickxel-macos-arm64.zip Unzip, move Chickxel.app to the Applications folder, then double-click it
macOS 12 or later, Intel Chickxel-macos-x64.zip Same as above
To see which chip your Mac has, open Apple menu → About This Mac. Changes from earlier versions are listed on the releases page.
Installing from the terminal
macOS — paste this into Terminal to download the file for your chip, install it to /Applications/Chickxel.app and launch it.
ARCH=$(uname -m); [ "$ARCH" = x86_64 ] && ARCH=x64
curl -fL -o /tmp/Chickxel.zip "https://github.com/1000Pro-1997/Chickxel/releases/latest/download/Chickxel-macos-$ARCH.zip" \
  && rm -rf /Applications/Chickxel.app && ditto -x -k /tmp/Chickxel.zip /Applications \
  && xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Chickxel.app; rm -f /tmp/Chickxel.zip; open /Applications/Chickxel.app
Windows — paste this into PowerShell to install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Chickxel, create a Start menu shortcut and launch it.
$d = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Chickxel"; $z = "$env:TEMP\Chickxel.zip"; $x = "$env:TEMP\Chickxel-x"
Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/1000Pro-1997/Chickxel/releases/latest/download/Chickxel-windows-x64.zip" -OutFile $z
Expand-Archive $z $x -Force; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $d | Out-Null
Copy-Item "$x\Chickxel-windows-x64\Chickxel.exe" $d -Force; Unblock-File "$d\Chickxel.exe"; Remove-Item $z, $x -Recurse -Force
$s = (New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell).CreateShortcut("$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Chickxel.lnk"); $s.TargetPath = "$d\Chickxel.exe"; $s.Save()
Start-Process "$d\Chickxel.exe"
Both methods install to a location your account can write to, so later updates happen automatically inside the app.

Dithering mixes two palette colors in light intensity (linear light) and compares the mix with the source in OKLab to set the ratio (e.g. a half black, half white pattern stands for sRGB 188 gray); it is used only when the mix is still closer to the source than the nearest single color after adding how visible the pattern is (lightness difference counts fully, hue and chroma differences half). Colors within a just-noticeable difference (OKLab 0.02) of a palette color are not dithered. ⑪ A before/after preview and ⑫ the change in color count are shown; alpha is kept and fully transparent pixels are left alone. Dragging the end of an effect box in the timeline's effect row to change its frame range, and dragging its body to move the whole range
Layer effects are non-destructive: they're applied only when displayed, without changing cel pixels. They automatically apply to anything you draw later and are all rendered per pixel (no blur or anti-aliasing).
Right-click menu of the Body layer name with Effects… (2), and the fx mark in the name cell
① Effects… · ② fx mark
Right-click a layer name and choose ① Effects… to open the effects dialog. Layers with effects show ② fx on the right of the name.
Normal layers and parts apply effects to their cel; groups apply them to the combined shape of their parts. For example, a group outline is drawn as a single line around the whole character.
Effects stack from the top of the list down (outline → shadow means the shadow includes the outline) and can be toggled individually.
Each effect has a frame range ("All frames" or a start–end frame).
Effect types
Effect What it does
Outline 1–3px thick, 4 or 8 directions, outside or inside. Color mode: a fixed color, or Shade from neighbors (each line pixel is the touching sprite pixel's color made darker or lighter by Shade −100 to +100% — dark blue next to blue, dark grey next to grey). Turn on Hide original (outline only) to erase the sprite and keep just the line (inside: only the edge ring). Effects clipped to this outline apply to the line only
Shadow Places a copy of the image's shape behind it, offset by X/Y. Dither (25%, 50%, 75%) gives pixel-art style shadows
Edge light and shade Light color on the edges facing the light (8 directions), shade color on the opposite side
Color overlay Blends a solid color or gradient with normal, multiply or screen. The gradient's "Whole sprite, one color (over time)" mode shifts the whole image through the stop colors over the effect range, with speed and ping-pong settings (formerly the gradient map effect)
Inner glow Blends a color from the edge inward by 1–8px
Color replace (palette swap) A list of "from color → to color" pairs. For turning red clothes blue without changing the cel
Hue adjust Grayscale, sepia, hue shift, brightness/contrast, saturation
Reflection Places a flipped copy below (floor/water), above (ceiling), left or right (wall). Height (width for sides), opacity, dither, tint, ripple
The following are animated effects that change over their frame range. A longer range makes them slower and a shorter one faster. They all share Speed (fast start, constant, slow start, slow start and end) and Loop (once, repeat N times, ping-pong N times).
Effect What it does
Explode Pixels burst outward in pieces and vanish. Distance, center, randomness, gravity, piece size, flash, seed
Light sweep A band of light sweeps diagonally across the image (the glint on coins or buttons)
Squash and stretch Wobbles like jelly, then returns to its original shape
Hit flash Flashes a single color (white, red, etc.) 1–8 times
Blink Repeatedly shows and hides (invincibility frames). Fully transparent, semi-transparent or dither 50%
Shake Shakes horizontally, vertically or both by whole pixels
Bob Smoothly floats up and down (floating items). Start and end connect seamlessly
Appear / disappear Opacity, dither, wipe (from top, bottom, left or right), pixel scatter
Fade in/out Changes the whole image's opacity between 0 and the original
Melt Each column drips downward and disappears (stretch or vanish)
Rotate Rotates around an anchor (pivot, center, bottom center). Uses RotSprite so pixel lines break less
Afterimage Places previous frames' images behind, gradually fainter (count, spacing, tint)
Color cycle Rotates through the colors in a list (water, fire, neon)
Shockwave ring A pixel ring spreads out from the center
Hologram Single-color shaded image + scanlines, bright band, flicker, glitch, edge glow
Effect colors and clipping

③ Color swatch · ④ Solid color / Gradient · ⑤ Clip to effect above

Each color setting can be a ④ solid color / gradient. For gradients, choose static / animated (the band moves or rotates over the range) for each of linear, radial, square and angular, and set the direction, count and angle. Stop editing, the Color space (RGB / HSL / OKLab / OKLCH; new gradients use OKLCH) and the right-click presets on the bar work as in the gradient tool; picking a preset in an effect also applies its shape, angle, direction, repeat and animation.
Turn on ⑤ Apply to → Clip to effect above to apply only to pixels changed by the previous effect. Example: clipping a Color overlay under an Outline gives a gradient outline.
Color popup opened from a color swatch: square picker, mode tabs, palette and eyedropper

Status Cause and fix
Missing source The project doesn't contain the source. Open the same JS file to draw it again.
Not allowed The script isn't allowed to run. Click Allow to run in the settings.
Source error The source has syntax or declaration errors. Fix them in the editor.
Failed A frame went over the limits (2 seconds, 50 million statements, 256 MB of memory) or the script threw an error. Only this effect is skipped on that frame.
Stopped It failed 3 times in a row, so computing stopped. Fix it, then click Run again in the settings or turn the effect off and on.

pages.text:
The Asset Manager installs, turns on and off, and removes asset packages (.chickxel-asset) that bundle effect recipes, gradients and script effects. It also downloads packages from the online list and exports or publishes your own personal assets.
Open it with Tools > Asset Manager….
The Asset Manager button on the Custom tab of the effects dialog opens it filtered to effects, and the Asset Manager button under the list in the Presets window opens it filtered to gradients. Show in Asset Manager in a Custom tab tile's right-click menu opens it with that asset selected.
Installed tab
Installed tab of the Asset Manager: filters, search and the import, export and publish buttons at the top; personal assets and installed packages on the left; details and buttons of the selected package on the right
① Tabs (Installed, Browse, Updates) · ② Kind filter and name search · ③ Import from File, Export Personal Assets, Publish Online · ④ List · ⑤ Details and buttons of the selected item
① There are Installed, Browse and Updates tabs.
② Filter by All / Effects / Gradients and search by name. Effects shows effect recipes and script effects together.
③ Import from File… checks and installs a .chickxel-asset file (a newer version of an installed package updates it). Export Personal Assets… bundles the personal assets shown in the list into one package file, and Publish Online… builds a public package to submit to the online catalog.
④ The list shows Personal assets, Installed packages with their assets, and Recently deleted packages, in that order.
⑤ Shows the details and buttons of the selected item, as listed in the table.
Selected item What it shows and its buttons
Package Status, ID, version, author, license, required app version, source, install time and contents. Turn Off/Turn On, Export as Package File…, Roll Back to Previous Version (updated packages only), Open File Location, Open Web Page (when the author has a website), View License (when there is a license file), Delete
Asset Preview (effects animate on a sample image, gradients show a strip), kind, source, author; for recipes, the effect list, insert range and parameters. Personal assets: Rename…, Edit parameters (recipes), Export as Package File…, Publish Online…, Delete. Package assets: Copy to Personal Assets. Gradients also have a favorite button
Recently deleted packages Deletion time. Kept for 30 days; Restore reinstalls it during that time
Recipes and gradients of a package that is off disappear from the Custom tab of the effects dialog, the gradient menu and Presets window, and the AI tool list (the files stay) and come back when you turn it on. Effects and gradients already inserted into projects are copied by value, so turning off or deleting the package doesn't change them.
Importing from a file checks the file list, sizes, checksums, effect settings and preview images before installing. If anything is wrong, each problem is listed and nothing is installed; a package that needs a newer Chickxel tells you which version it needs.
On first launch, your old custom effects and gradient presets move into personal assets. The old files stay in the settings folder as effect-presets.backup-date.json and gradient-presets.backup-date.json.
Browse tab
Browse tab: filters, search, tags and Refresh at the top; online package list on the left; preview, information and Install button of the selected package on the right
⑥ Filters, search, tags, Refresh · ⑦ Online package list · ⑧ Details of the selected package and Install
⑥ The online list is downloaded from the website the first time you open the tab ("Loading the online list…" while loading, then "N packages · list from time"). It has the All / Effects / Gradients filter, search (name, description, author, tags), the All tags list and Refresh.
⑦ Each row shows the name, version, author, contents (numbers of effect recipes, gradients and script effects) and status (installed version, new version, or can't be installed on this version).
⑧ Preview image, short description, ID, version, installed version, author, license, contents, required app version, size, published, updated, review (Official Chickxel / Reviewed) and tags, with Install (or Update to …, Show in Installed) and Open Web Page.
Install shows a progress bar, percentage and Cancel in its place. If the downloaded file doesn't match the checksum in the list, only an error is shown and nothing changes. A package that can't be used on this version shows why (for example "Can't install: requires Chickxel 1.20.0 or later") and its Install button is off. Packages installed online have the source Online catalog.
Official packages hold one asset each: 8 gradients (Rainbow, Repeating Rainbow, Sunset, Ocean, Transparent Fade, Fire, Forest, Grayscale) and 3 effect recipes (Outlined Drop Shadow, Hit Reaction, Shiny Pickup).
Updates tab
Check for updates downloads the online list again and shows, for each package with a newer version, an "Installed 1.0.0 → new version 1.1.0" row and an Update to … button. New versions are installed only when you click; the previous version is kept for rollback, and effects already in your projects don't change. The tab name shows the number of updates (e.g. Updates (1)); with none, it says "All installed packages are up to date."
Without an internet connection, the Browse and Updates tabs say in orange that the online list couldn't be reached and show the last downloaded list instead. Installed assets keep working.
Using package assets
The Custom tab of the effects dialog shows recipes from enabled packages after your personal recipes (see Effect recipes).
In the gradient Presets window, package gradients show the package name next to their name, and Rename and Delete are off. Edit one and click Save as Personal Asset to keep the original and create a personal copy (see Gradient).
To modify a package asset, make a personal copy with Copy to Personal Assets in its details.
Publish Online
Bundle personal assets into a public package, check it, save it and open the online catalog submission form. Publish Online… at the top of the Installed tab starts with the personal asset selected in the list (or, with none selected, all personal assets shown in the list); Publish Online… in a personal asset's details opens the Publish Online window with that asset checked. If you saved the same assets before, that package information and asset selection are filled in again.
Author: author ID (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; the first part of the package ID, which can't change after publishing), display name and website (optional). Remembered on this computer for your next publish and for personal exports.
Package: name, package ID (follows "author-id.name" unless you edit it), version, short description (up to 200 characters) and tags (comma-separated). If the ID was published before, the last version and a suggested next version appear under the version field; Use suggested version fills it in.
License: choose CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC-BY-NC-4.0, MIT or Apache-2.0 to see a one-line summary. Custom needs a license ID starting with LicenseRef- and the license text.
Included assets: checklist of personal assets (checked ones first) with "M of N personal assets".
List preview: the image shown in Browse. Pick one of the included assets' previews or use a PNG (up to 512×512, 1 MB) with Replace with Image File….
Pre-upload check: checked as you type, with the same rules as the online catalog. Red X = error (blocks saving), orange exclamation mark = warning (you can still save).
With no errors, a blue check says all checks passed and Save and Open Submission Page… turns on. Click it.
Choose where to save. Chickxel saves <ID>-<version>.chickxel-asset and <ID>-<version>-submission.zip in the same folder, shows the zip in your file manager and opens the GitHub asset submission form in your browser with the package information filled in.
Drag the zip file into the form and submit it. Chickxel uploads nothing itself; submitted packages appear in Browse after review.
Main errors: author ID, display name or website (https) format; package ID, version (SemVer), name, short description or tag format; missing license or license text; the personal-export author; a package ID whose first part differs from the author ID; the official-only author ID chickxel; no list preview; and, compared with the last downloaded online list, changed contents for the same version, a lower version or a name clashing with another package. Warnings: no tags, an uncommon license ID, or the same version saved on this computer with different contents.
Export Personal Assets… and Export as Package File… make personal packages that can't be published online. They use the display name remembered in the Publish Online window as the author name.

pages.text:
File Role
.chickxel The editable source. Layers, effects, frames, tags, parts, skins, outfit presets and export settings are all stored only here.
Exported images (PNG) The output, used in Unity or other programs.
.meta Unity settings (sprite cells, pivot, etc.).
.spriteLib Unity Sprite Library. Created only when turned on (see Parts · skins).
.chickxel-asset Asset package. Bundles effect recipes, gradients and script effects for installing and sharing with the Asset Manager.
Projects saved by this version use a new .chickxel format (format version 4) that stores effects by stable type IDs, so older versions of Chickxel can't open them. Older projects and custom effects open as before. Effects this version doesn't know (for example, ones added in a newer Chickxel) aren't drawn but are kept when you save, and script effect sources are saved inside the project file (see Script effects).

Multi-frame images are inserted without transform mode.

Each band counts color edges that continue over several rows, drops short 1–2 px noise and weights high-contrast edges more, so sharp, continuous edges are matched first. A checked step tries everything it can change — Background: remove sticker border · Grid: pixel size, size jitter, pixel size source, local cell correction (with max shift and band in trials that use it) and a manual grid's offset X/Y · Cell color: cell color method, ignored cell border, transparency threshold, color snap step · Palette: palette method (all five, plus an existing palette when starting from one), color count, grouping range, group radius, palette colors, edge cell weight, color distance, keep distinct hues, prefer shade family, dither, snap outline color, outline darkness · Cleanup: cleanup on/off, outline fit mode, vector simplify, keep small blobs. Values tied to a method change only in trials using that method, and a palette method or dither with
on is never changed. The pixel size is never shrunk without evidence:

searches only within ±15% of the source outline thickness; otherwise the search sweeps between the three estimates and their 2×, 3×, ½ and ⅓, going down only to 0.75× of the starting size and the auto estimate (smaller cells always improve fidelity, which would make results needlessly large). An exact multiple of a clean image keeps its pixel size. The pixel size is changed through
for an auto grid, the pixel size for a manual grid and the factor for scale-factor output; a fixed output size skips it.

It first tries each item on its own (7 spread-out values for numbers, every value for choices), then climbs from the best few points with small steps (shrinking the step when nothing improves). Identical settings are never run twice, and background removal and frame splitting are done once, so the trials run quickly on several threads.

) ends with no further improvement, the same search runs again from the best result. A new pass also climbs from the top result not yet used as a start whose settings differ most from the best and from a small fixed nudge of the best, so it doesn't get stuck in one spot. A pass that raises the best score by less than 0.1 points doesn't stop the search right away: up to three more passes start from other top results and wider nudges before it stops, so optimizing an already optimized result doesn't give up after its first pass. Settings already tried are never run again. The same image and settings always give the same result when the run ends on the trial budget rather than the time limit.
, whichever comes first (one budget shared by all passes of that preset; 2000 trials and 120 seconds for a new preset). With
on and other steps optimized too, the grid stage uses up to half of it.

On the bundled sample (default settings, the earlier default items and budget — pixel size, color count, cell color method, cleanup and palette colors; 200 trials, 60 s) it took about 3 s and 162 trials to go from 70.3 to 80.8 (cells about 16.1 → 14.9 px, 26 colors, fill holes off, palette colors kept as original colors, 99% of outline pixels 1 px).

The pixel size is never shrunk without evidence: By shrinking searches only within ±15% of the source outline thickness; otherwise the search sweeps between the three estimates and their 2×, 3×, ½ and ⅓, going down only to 0.75× of the starting size and the auto estimate (smaller cells always improve fidelity, which would make results needlessly large). An exact multiple of a clean image keeps its pixel size. The pixel size is changed through Add to auto pixel size (px) for an auto grid, the pixel size for a manual grid and the factor for scale-factor output; a fixed output size skips it.
Search method and stopping conditions
It first tries each item on its own (7 spread-out values for numbers, every value for choices), then climbs from the best few points with small steps (shrinking the step when nothing improves). Identical settings are never run twice, and background removal and frame splitting are done once, so the trials run quickly on several threads.
When one search (a pass) ends with no further improvement, the same search runs again from the best result. A new pass also climbs from the top result not yet used as a start whose settings differ most from the best and from a small fixed nudge of the best, so it doesn't get stuck in one spot. A pass that raises the best score by less than 0.1 points doesn't stop the search right away: up to three more passes start from other top results and wider nudges before it stops, so optimizing an already optimized result doesn't give up after its first pass. Settings already tried are never run again. The same image and settings always give the same result when the run ends on the trial budget rather than the time limit.
Each preset stops at the Trials or Seconds of its 0. Optimize criteria, whichever comes first (one budget shared by all passes of that preset; 2000 trials and 120 seconds for a new preset). With Optimize grid fit first on and other steps optimized too, the grid stage uses up to half of it.
On the bundled sample (default settings, the earlier default items and budget — pixel size, color count, cell color method, cleanup and palette colors; 200 trials, 60 s) it took about 3 s and 162 trials to go from 70.3 to 80.8 (cells about 16.1 → 14.9 px, 26 colors, fill holes off, palette colors kept as original colors, 99% of outline pixels 1 px).

runs.t: Ask the Codex tab for something like "draw a knight with a sword", and instead of placing pixels one by one the AI calls the

(under Draw pixels directly — shown for Auto and Draw pixels directly, off by default, saved): when on, the colors the AI paints with the pixel tools (the draw_pixels legend, set_pixels, draw_shape, fill, replace_color's target color, the new_project background) are changed to the nearest color of the

(the same color distance as the Pixelate tool). Fully transparent (erasing) is still allowed; semi-transparent colors become the nearest opaque palette color. The tool result tells the AI what changed, e.g. "팔레트 색으로 맞춤: #E63228→#C81E1E", and each message also sends the palette colors (up to 64) so the AI draws with them from the start. It works in both the Claude and Codex tabs and doesn't affect generated images (the conversion's palette settings) or layer effects. When off, all colors and alpha are used as before.

: with Draw pixels directly (including Auto's fallback), the AI first reads your words and attached images together, lists the subject, size, proportions, pose, colors, style and anything to avoid, and plans the overall layout and where each part goes. Without an image, it works from the conditions you described. When a turn that changed pixels or parts ends, Chickxel automatically sends the AI the current canvas with all layers combined for a review. The AI scores the silhouette, limb placement and style out of 10 against your original request and images, fixes what's wrong, and looks at the whole picture again (up to three rounds of fixes; if it doesn't improve, it explains the remaining problems). The score is the AI's subjective judgment, not an exact similarity measurement. The review and fixes belong to the same undo step as the turn, and the extra AI turns take more time and usage. Generate image → pixelate doesn't use this review.

pages.text:
Ask the Codex tab for something like "draw a knight with a sword", and instead of placing pixels one by one the AI calls the generate_pixel_art tool. Chickxel runs the Codex CLI on your computer (codex exec, Codex image generation) with your ChatGPT login (no API key) to generate a high-quality image, then turns it into pixel art the same way as Pixelate AI images (background removal, auto optimize, a shared palette and 1-px outlines) and inserts it. Each image takes about 30–90 seconds.
The drawing settings panel opened in the Codex tab (Draw pixels directly chosen)
① Drawing settings button (a red X while open) · ② Codex CLI status · ③ Info icon · ④ Auto · ⑤ Generate image → pixelate · ⑥ Draw pixels directly · ⑦ Use palette colors only
Drawing settings: the ① Drawing settings button (sliders icon) next to the question mark button at the top of the chat window opens a settings panel on the right, like the help panel. Only one of help and drawing settings is open at a time, and while it's open the button shows a red X. The panel also shows the ② Codex CLI status (logged in / not installed / not logged in).
Hover over an option or its ③ info icon for the longer explanation. Generate image shows only the generation options, Draw pixels directly shows only Use palette colors only, and Auto shows both.
Drawing mode: ④ Auto (default) in the Codex tab edits the current picture by placing pixels when the chat's Current file only is on, and otherwise tries Generate image → pixelate first. If it can't generate (no Codex CLI or a generation error), the same request is drawn with the pixel tools, followed by the same whole-picture review as Draw pixels directly. If you press Stop during generation, it doesn't fall back to drawing pixels. ⑤ Generate image → pixelate always generates and converts, and ⑥ Draw pixels directly has the AI place pixels one by one with the pixel tools. If you choose ⑤ or ⑥ yourself, that mode is kept. A Generate image setting saved by an older version switches to Auto once; a saved Draw pixels directly is kept.
⑦ Use palette colors only (under Draw pixels directly — shown for Auto and Draw pixels directly, off by default, saved): when on, the colors the AI paints with the pixel tools (the draw_pixels legend, set_pixels, draw_shape, fill, replace_color's target color, the new_project background) are changed to the nearest color of the active palette (the same color distance as the Pixelate tool). Fully transparent (erasing) is still allowed; semi-transparent colors become the nearest opaque palette color. The tool result tells the AI what changed, e.g. "팔레트 색으로 맞춤: #E63228→#C81E1E", and each message also sends the palette colors (up to 64) so the AI draws with them from the start. It works in both the Claude and Codex tabs and doesn't affect generated images (the conversion's palette settings) or layer effects. When off, all colors and alpha are used as before.
Whole-picture review when drawing pixels: with Draw pixels directly (including Auto's fallback), the AI first reads your words and attached images together, lists the subject, size, proportions, pose, colors, style and anything to avoid, and plans the overall layout and where each part goes. Without an image, it works from the conditions you described. When a turn that changed pixels or parts ends, Chickxel automatically sends the AI the current canvas with all layers combined for a review. The AI scores the silhouette, limb placement and style out of 10 against your original request and images, fixes what's wrong, and looks at the whole picture again (up to three rounds of fixes; if it doesn't improve, it explains the remaining problems). The score is the AI's subjective judgment, not an exact similarity measurement. The review and fixes belong to the same undo step as the turn, and the extra AI turns take more time and usage. Generate image → pixelate doesn't use this review.

Background: unless you mention a background, the image is generated on a plain transparent background with no scenery.
Generation option What it does
⑧ Result-size correction Off by default (older saved settings also load as off). When off, ordinary generated images are converted with the main preset's result-size setting (with Auto, at the pixel grid found in the image), and a size you mention in the chat (e.g. "64×64") or one Codex picks for the subject before generating is only passed to the image generation as a rough scale hint. A turn that converts an attached picture to pixel art fits the result to the chosen size even with correction off (see turning a reference image into pixel art below). When on, other generated images are also fitted to the Result size setting or the size given in the chat. View conversion settings opens with the conversion settings that made the result.
⑨ Result size 32 · 48 · 64 · Custom (long side in px). Only enabled when Result-size correction is on.
⑩ Remove background Removes the background when converting (on by default).
⑪ Auto-optimize the conversion Auto-optimizes the conversion and inserts the top-scoring result as-is (on by default). The conversion starts from the saved stage settings and optimization criteria of the AI image conversion preset — the preset whose Main button is green in the Auto optimize settings window (regardless of that preset's Auto optimize checkbox). If that preset is deleted, the built-in Same hue family preset is used while it exists, otherwise the first preset in the list. When this is off, the main preset's stage settings are still used and only the optimization is skipped. The progress reads "Optimizing conversion… pass p · trial n/N · best x". If the top result is a failed one (empty or too small — wrong pixel size detected), nothing is inserted and an error is reported.
⑫ Insert as New layer · New document.
⑬ Style reference Auto · None · Specific reference. A pixel-art example sent along with the generation. Auto picks one from your references (your own; built-in examples only when turned on) when you attach a non-pixel character picture to redraw as pixel art, or when a reference matches what is being drawn.
⑭ Default animation frames Idle 4 · Walk 6 · Run 6 · Attack 6 · Jump 6 · Hurt 3 · Death 5 (2–12). A count you give in the chat wins.
⑮ Generation (Animation group) All on one sheet (recommended) (default) · One image per frame (the previous behavior: one frame at a time with frame 1 and the previous frame attached). Choosing one image per frame shows a red warning: per-frame generation often changes the character's look and size between frames and takes as long as the number of frames.
The options are saved in the settings.

⑦ Add files… Adds several image or note files at once. You can also drag files onto the window.
⑧ Add current canvas Adds the open image as a reference.
⑨ Delete Moves the selected reference file to the app trash (built-in references can't be deleted).
⑩ Open folder Opens the references folder in Explorer/Finder.
⑪ Edit rules Opens your own style rules, rules.md (created from a template if missing). The AI reads them together with the default rules.
⑫ Caption with AI Puts a request to add titles, descriptions and tags to uncaptioned references into the input box of the active AI tab and brings up the chat window. It's sent only when you press send, so nothing is spent automatically.
When some references have no description, the window shows ⑬ "N references have no description". Descriptions and tags help the AI find them.
The kind filter list open
③ Kind filter (All kinds, Character, Item, Tile, Effect, UI, Other)
Asking: say something like "Draw a 32px bat like the slime in the references." and the AI looks up the references before drawing. The chat help (question-mark button) has a References tool group and this example.
Adding from the chat: say "save this to my references" and the AI adds the current canvas (or a layer or frame range) with a title, description and tags. Adding and captioning references only write to the library folder, so they work even with Current file only on.
The AI references tab in Preferences
⑭ References folder · ⑮ Change… · ⑯ Default · ⑰ Open folder · ⑱ Show built-in examples
Folder (⑭): by default <settings folder>/Chickxel/References (%AppData%\Chickxel\References on Windows). Files you put into this folder outside the app are picked up automatically when the window opens.
Supported files: images (.png, .gif with frames, .chickxel projects — each frame composited, animations keep their frame count) and text notes (.md, .txt). Title, description, tags, kind (character, item, tile, effect, UI, other), size, frame count, palette and similar info are stored in index.json in the same folder.
Built-in references (marked Built-in, can't be deleted): the style rule set Chickxel default rules (1 px or selective outline, a single light direction, 3–4-shade hue-shifted ramps, no orphan or jaggy pixels, a limited palette, a readable silhouette, consistent proportions, and key poses, smears and walk-cycle contacts for animation) and example images — a 16×16 slime, a 16×16 sword, a 32×32 front-facing character, a 4-frame 16×16 slime bounce, and a 16×16 grass tile.
Preferences: in Edit > Preferences… > AI references you can ⑮ Change… the ⑭ folder, go back to the ⑯ Default folder, ⑰ Open folder, and turn the built-in example images back on with ⑱ Show built-in examples (they are off by default for now because of their low quality; while off they are not used for search or as image-generation style references).
References stay on your computer. Chickxel uploads and downloads nothing; only the AI CLI you already use (Claude Code or Codex) sees what the AI fetches with its tools.

pages.title: Troubleshooting

blocks.alt: Codex tab: a red line explaining why the editor tools could not be reached, and an end line with only the time

runs.t: ① Red line with the likely reason · ② End line showing only the time (Codex)
If the AI can't connect to the editor, the chat shows a ① red line with the likely reason. Common causes are a proxy (
), VPN or security software blocking connections to 127.0.0.1, or an outdated CLI.
Codex replies appear all at once after they're fully written, and show only the ② time, not the cost (Claude shows the cost too).
If you distribute an app with this feature to others, check Anthropic's and OpenAI's usage policies (restrictions on using subscription logins in third-party apps).
